questions.question: Whose greatest achievement was the setting up of the Brahmo Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **3** i.e. __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__.

**Brahmo Samaj**

__
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is regarded as **Father of Modern India**.
 
• He was born in a well-to-do family in Bengal in 1772.
 
• He received his traditional Sanskrit learning at Banaras and Arabic and Persian learning at Patna.
 
• He made a deep study not only of Hinduism but also of Islam, Christianity and Judaism. 
 
• He started two newspapers, one in Bengali and another in Persian. He was given the **title of *Raja* **and sent to England by the Mughal Emperor as his envoy.
 
• He supported the introduction of English education in India, which was necessary to promote enlightenment and knowledge of science.
 
• **He was the founder of the first religious reform organisation i.e. Brahmo Samaj, founded in 1828**__. Hence option 3 is correct.
 
• He advocated belief in a universal religion based on the principle of one supreme God.
 
• He condemned idol-worship and the rites and rituals
 
• The two most prominent leader of the Brahmo Samaj was Debendranath Tagore and Keshab Chandra Sen.

questions.question: The Indian Federation is based on the pattern of__________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Federation is based on the pattern of **Canada**.

 
 
• Federalism in India refers to the relationship between the **Centre government and state governments **in India.
 
• Both the state and the Centre governments derive their authority from the constitution.
 
• **The Seventh Schedule** of the Indian constitution provides three lists for the distribution of legislative subjects between the state and Centre governments.
 
• The Centre government can make laws on the subjects in the **union list**.
 
• The state governments can make laws on the subjects in the **state list**.
 
• Both governments can make laws on the **concurrent list**.
 
• Subjects which is not mentioned in any of the three lists are known as** residuary subjects**.
 
• If there is any dispute between the two governments, the will of the central government prevails.
 
• The constitution has empowered the central government to make a change in the boundaries of the states.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The important features borrowed from the **American(USA) constitution** are:

 
 
• Fundamental rights.
 
• Judicial review.
 
• Preamble.
 
• Impeachment.
 
 
 
• The important features borrowed from the **Russian (USSR) constitution** are:
 
 
• Fundamental duties.
 
• Five-year plan.

questions.question: A ______ is a substance composed of two or more elements which are chemically combined.
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **two or more different types** of **elements** are **chemically mixed** in a specific ratio, the resultant substance is called a **compound**.

**Elements:**

 
• Any compound that **cannot be broken down into simpler chemicals** by regular chemical processes is referred to as a chemical element or **element**.
 
• The **building blocks** of which all **matter** is made are called **elements**.

**Chemical Combination:**

 
• The **underlying rules **that underlie interactions between **atoms and molecules**. 
 
• Interactions that can involve a broad number of combinations that can take place in a variety of ways are described by **chemical combinations**.
 
• A staggering variety of chemical reactions and molecules are made possible by this extraordinary diversity of interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**Matter:**

 
• Anything that **fills space** and has **mass** is referred to as **matter**. 
 
• In other words, the matter is the "**stuff**" that the cosmos is made of.
 
• **Elements** are the **fundamental building blocks** of all **matter**.
 
• They possess unique chemical and physical characteristics and cannot be converted into other elements through regular chemical processes.

**Substance:**

 
• A kind of matter with predictable chemical composition and physical properties is referred to as a **chemical substance**.
 
• According to certain references, a chemical substance **cannot be physically divided** into its **component** parts without **rupturing chemical bonds**.

**Gas:**

 
• A state of matter composed of particles without a **specified volume or shape** is referred to as a **gas**.
 
• **Solids, liquids, and plasma**, it is one of the four basic states of matter.

questions.question: Under which Article can the Parliament amend the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Under the **Article 368**, the parliament can **amend the Constitution**.

 
• **Amending the constitution of India** is the process of making amendments to the fundamental law or supreme law of the country.
 
• The amendment process in the constitution is set out in** Part XX (Article 368) of the Indian Constitution. **
 
• This procedure preserves the sanctity of India's Constitution and holds a check on the Indian Parliament's arbitrary power.
 
• Article 368 does not set down the legislative process to be followed at various points of the amendment.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding the Constituent Assembly of India is ***not ***correct?

options.text: The Constituent Assembly was composed of members who had been elected indirectly by the Members of the Provincial Legislative Assembly.
The Constituent Assembly held its first sitting on 9th December, 1946
The seats in each province were distributed among the three main communities-Muslims, Sikhs and General, in proportion to their respective populations.
The method of selection in the case of representatives of Indian States was to be determined by the Governor-General of India.

questions.solution:
Option __**4 **__is not correct, i.e __**The method of selection in the case of representatives of Indian States was to be determined by the Governor-General of India.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The Constituent Assembly was constituted in **November 1946** under the scheme formulated by the **Cabinet Mission Plan**.
 
• The **features** of the scheme were:
 
 
• The **total strength** of the Constituent Assembly was to be** 389**. Of these, **296 seats** were to be allotted to **British India** and **93 seats** to the **princely states**.
 
• Each province and princely state (or group of states in case of small states) was to be **allotted seats in proportion to their respective population**. Roughly, one seat was to be allotted for every million population.
 
• **Seats allocated to each British province** were to be **divided among the three principal communities–Muslims, Sikhs and General** (all except Muslims and Sikhs), **in proportion to their population.**
 
• The **representatives of each community were to be elected by members of that community** in the provincial legislative assembly and voting was to be by the method of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The **representatives of the princely states were to be nominated by the heads of the princely states.**
 
 
 
• It is, thus, clear that the **Constituent Assembly** was to be a **partly elected and partly nominated body**.
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** held its **first meeting on December 9, 1946**.
 
• The **Muslim League boycotted** the meeting and insisted on a separate state of Pakistan. The meeting was, thus, attended by only 211 members.
 
• **Dr Sachchidananda Sinha**, the oldest member, was elected as the **temporary President** of the Assembly, following the **French practice**.

questions.question: The tissue that connects one bone with the other is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ligament__**.

__
 
• A Ligament is a fibrous connective tissue, which connects **bone to another bone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 Adipose tissue
 
 __
 
• Adipose tissue is a specialized connective tissue consisting of lipid-rich cells called adipocytes.
 
• The main function of adipose tissue is to store energy in the form of lipids (fat).
 
• There are three types of adipose tissue: white, brown, and beige adipose.
 
 
• White adipose stores energy and helps to insulate the body.
 
• Brown and beige adipose tissue burn energy and generate heat.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Cartilage
 
 
 
• Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue that keeps joint motion fluid by coating the surfaces of the bones in joints and by cushioning bones against impact.
 
 
 
 

 Epithelium
 
 
 
• They form the covering of all body surfaces, line body cavities and hollow organs, and are the major tissue in glands.
 
• Functions of epithelial cells include secretion, selective absorption, protection, transcellular transport, and sensing.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• There are 3 types of bone tissue:
 
 
• **Compact** tissue: The **harder, outer tissue of bones**.
 
• **Cancellous** tissue: The **sponge-like tissue inside bones**.
 
• **Subchondral** tissue: The **smooth tissue at the ends of bones**, which is **covered** with another type of tissue called **cartilage**.

questions.question: Which event led to the termination of Non-Cooperation - Khilafat Movement by Gandhiji?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option** __4,__ **i.e** __Chauri- Chaura incident__.**

 
 

 Passing of Rowlatt Act
 
 
 
• Known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919**.
 
• It was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919.
 
• The Act gave them the power to **arrest any person without any trial**.
 
 
 
 

 Death of Bal Gangadhar Tilak
 
 
 
• His famous declaration “**Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it**”.
 
• The British Government termed him as the "**Father of Indian Unrest**".
 
 
 
 

 Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
 
 
 
• On **13th April 1919**, a British military officer, **General Dyer**, ordered his troops to fire at the people gathering at Jallianwala Bagh (Amritsar) to protest against the arrest of the two nationalist leaders, **Satya Pal and Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew**.
 
 
 
 

 **Chauri- Chaura incident**
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation movement** was started by Gandhi in 1920 to drive the Britishers out of the country and the Khilafat movement was an agitation by Indian Muslims, allied with Indian nationalists to force the British government to undo the injustice done to the Sultan of Turkey.
 
• **Chauri Chaura** incident led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation - Khilafat Movement.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is*** incorrect*** with respect to anti-defection law?

options.text: It was inserted in the Constitution through 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1985.
Anti defection law is not applicable on nominated members as they are not elected by the people.
An independent member can be disqualified if he joined a political party after elections within 6 months

questions.solution:
Option **2** is **incorrect**.

 
• Anti Defection Law was inserted in the Constitution in 1985 through the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act.
 
• According to the tenth schedule of Anti Defection Law, a legislator can be disqualified by the presiding officer of the legislature for being a member of the House,
 
 
• If he voluntarily gives up his membership of such political party; or
 
• If he votes against any direction issued by his political party without obtaining prior permission of such party and such an act has not been condoned by the party within 15 days.
 
• If a member has been elected as “Independent”, he/she would be disqualified if he/she joined another political party after the elections.
 
• **If a nominated member joins a party six months after he becomes a member of the legislature**.

questions.question: Which is the only continent through which the Tropic of Cancer, Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn passes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Africa**__.

 
• Longitude and Latitude- Latitude and longitude are imaginary lines and are used to define any location on earth. Latitude is the angular distance of a point on the surface, from the central part of the Earth. While lines joining the North Pole to the South Pole are called longitude lines earth is divided into a total of 360 longitude lines. Longitude and latitude both measure in degrees.

 Important lines of Latitude-

 
• Equator-Equator represents the zero degrees latitude line it is an imaginary line running on the globe divides it into two equal parts. The northern half of the earth is known as the Northern Hemisphere and the southern half is known as the Southern Hemisphere The Equator passes through South America, Asia, and Africa.
 
• Tropic of Cancer- It is a line of latitude 23½° N in the Northern Hemisphere. It passes through Africa, Asia, and North America.
 
• Tropic of Capricorn- It is a line of latitude 23½° S in the Southern Hemisphere. It passes through South America, Africa, and Australia.

Hence, Africa is the only continent, in which tropic of cancer, equator, and tropic of Capricorn passes through.

questions.question: Vibrating in the same phase, the distance between any two nearest particles of the medium is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1** i.e. __**Wavelength**__.

__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• **Wavelength:** The space or length between two successive crests or troughs of a wave is called the wavelength.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bc73a3078186f11a5b5eb735863b0975e3720858151c33bebbb537f8c916141.png] 

 
• It is our well known primary physical quantity known as Length.
 
• Wavelength is represented by the Greek letter lambda (λ). 

​**EXPLANATION__**:

 
• Vibrating in the same phase, the **distance between any two nearest particles of the medium is the wavelength**. So option 1 is correct.
 
• **Frequency**: It is the number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit of time. Its SI unit is Hertz (Hz).
 
• **Velocity: **Velocity is defined as the rate of change of displacement of a body with respect to time. The SI unit is meter per second (ms⁻¹).

​__**EXTRA POINTS**__:

 
• Angstrom (Å), unit of length used chiefly in measuring wavelengths of light, equal to 10-10 meter, or 0.1 nanometers.
 
• It is named for the 19th-century Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström.

 
• **Frequency** and **wavelength** are inversely proportional to each other.

​Velocity (v) = frequency (f) × wavelength (λ)

questions.question: "Passing of like qualities from one generation to the next" is the definition of which of the following?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is heredity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **__Hint__**

**Heredity: **

__
 
• It** **is the transmission of genetic characteristics (traits) from parents to offspring.
 
• As a result, the offspring look similar in some aspects to parents.
 
• Heredity takes place through reproduction.
 
• Traits may be - color, height, skin complexion, etc. 

**Reproduction:** 

 
• It is the process by which (parent) organisms give rise to new young ones (offspring).
 
• Reproduction is either asexual or asexual.
 
• In asexually reproducing organisms offspring looks identical to parents like plants and bacteria
 
• However, in sexually reproducing organisms variation (differences in traits) arise in offspring.

**Inheritance:**

 
• Process of transfer of genetic traits and their expression from one to another generation.
 
• Genetic information is stored in the DNA, which can be passed on to the next generation through reproduction..

**Explanation**__

 
 

 
 
Concept

 
 
 
Meaning

 
 
 

 
 
Variation

 
 
 
The degree by which progeny differs from their parents. In simple words differences in characters of individuals.

 
 
 

 
 
Hereditary

 
 
 
The trait or character that can be transferred from one generation to the next.

 
 
 

 
 
Inheritance

 
 
 
The process by which the transfer of characters from parent to offspring takes place.

 
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

 
• Please note that 'heredity' and 'hereditary' are words with different meanings.
 
• **'Heredity'** refers to the **process of transfer of characters** from one generation to another.
 
• Whereas, **'hereditary'** refers to the **character that can be transferred** from one generation to another.
 
• For example, haemophilia is a hereditary disease, meaning it can be transmitted by heredity.
